mainTopic: Who may slaughter: the impure slaughterer's knife, and the readings of the משנה by אביי (כותי under supervision), רבא (a Jew going in and out), and רב אשי (ישראל משומד)
overview: This amud starts in the middle of a challenge. A person who is impure from a מת is an אב הטומאה, so he should make his metal knife impure ('חרב הרי הוא כחלל'), and the knife would then make the meat impure. The גמרא gives two answers. In the first, his impurity came from a שרץ, which cannot pass to the knife. In the second, he slaughtered with a reed stalk, which cannot become impure. Then אביי reads the משנה as being about a כותי: he may slaughter from the start only when a Jew stands over him. If he slaughtered without that, he is given a כזית of the meat to see whether he eats it. רבא challenges this and proves from a משנה about guarding wine that a Jew going in and out is enough from the start. So he gives his own reading of the משנה. Both readings run into the same question: what case do the words 'וכולן ששחטו' refer to? Both end with קשיא. Finally, רב אשי reads 'הכל שוחטין' as including a ישראל משומד who eats נבילות לתיאבון, in line with a ruling of רבא that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The knife itself becomes impure and passes it to the meat
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the idea that a טמא can slaughter pure meat with a long knife. A person impure from a מת is an אב הטומאה, so he makes the metal knife impure, and the knife then makes the meat impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: A metal sword is like the corpse it touches. This person is a primary source of impurity, so he should make the knife impure, and then the knife should go and make the meat impure!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer it just gave. Holding a long knife does not help, because the knife itself becomes impure from the person holding it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a rule that metal touching a source of impurity takes on that same strong level of impurity ('חרב הרי הוא כחלל'). So if the slaughterer is an אב הטומאה, the knife becomes an אב הטומאה too. Not touching the meat with his hand does not help, since the knife touches the meat anyway.

keyTerms.meaning: A metal sword or utensil takes on the same impurity level as the corpse (or impure person) it touches
A primary source of impurity, strong enough to make people and utensils impure
Knife
Let him make it impure

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the problem is the person touching the meat. The case already had him avoid touching it. The problem is that the metal knife becomes just as impure as he is.

phrases.english: A sword is like a corpse,
phrases.notes: From the words 'חלל חרב' in במדבר 19:16: metal that touches impurity takes on the same strong impurity.

phrases.english: he is a primary source of impurity,
phrases.notes: He means the slaughterer, who became impure from a dead body.

phrases.english: so let him make the knife impure,
and the knife goes and makes the meat impure!

steps.triggerLanguage: חֶרֶב הֲרֵי הוּא כֶּחָלָל, אַב הַטּוּמְאָה הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the challenge to the previous answer, which said a טמא may slaughter with a long knife without touching the meat.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that a טמא can slaughter pure meat by using a long knife and not touching the meat.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The metal knife takes on the person's אב הטומאה status, so it makes the meat impure no matter how long it is.

steps.title: He became impure from a creeping animal
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the slaughterer became impure from a שרץ. That makes him only a first-level impure person, and he cannot make the knife impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the case is where he became impure from a creeping animal.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes the problem by changing the kind of impurity the slaughterer has. If his impurity came from a שרץ, the knife stays pure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone who touches a שרץ is only first-level impure, not an אב הטומאה. A first-level impure person cannot make utensils impure, so the 'חרב הרי הוא כחלל' rule does not apply. The knife stays pure and the meat stays pure.

keyTerms.meaning: A creeping animal (one of eight listed in the תורה) whose dead body causes impurity
He became impure
Rather, introducing a corrected version of the case

phrases.english: Rather, where he became impure through a creeping animal,
phrases.notes: Impurity from a שרץ is a weaker level, so the person can't pass it on to the knife.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 1 by narrowing the kind of impurity involved.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case (אוקימתא) to a weaker kind of impurity
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We assumed the slaughterer was impure from a מת, which would make the knife impure.
steps.terutzMaskana: He is impure from a שרץ. He cannot make utensils impure, so the knife and the meat stay pure.

steps.title: Or he slaughtered with a reed stalk
steps.stepSummary: A second answer: even if he is impure from a מת, he slaughtered with a reed stalk, which cannot become impure. A ברייתא proves that slaughtering with a reed is allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you want, say: really he became impure from a corpse, but he checked a reed stalk and slaughtered with it. As a ברייתא teaches: one may slaughter with anything, whether with flint, glass, or a reed stalk.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives another way out. It keeps the strong impurity from a מת but changes the tool, so nothing can carry the impurity to the meat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem in step 1 depended on the knife being metal. A reed stalk is not metal and cannot become impure, so it cannot pass impurity to the meat. The ברייתא shows that a reed stalk really is a valid tool for שחיטה, as long as it was checked to be smooth.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you wish, say, introducing a second, alternative answer
Actually, keeping the original assumption
The sharp outer stalk of a reed
Flint, a sharp stone
Glass

steps.whatToRemember: The challenge came from metal passing on impurity. One answer weakens the person's impurity (שרץ), and the other changes the tool to something that cannot become impure (a reed).

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:
actually, he became impure through a corpse,
and the case is where he checked a reed stalk
phrases.notes: He checked that the reed's edge was smooth with no nicks, as any slaughtering tool must be.

phrases.english: and slaughtered with it,
as it is taught: one may slaughter with anything,
whether with flint or with glass,
or with a reed stalk.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי בָּעֵית אֵימָא: לְעוֹלָם דְּאִיטַּמִּי בְּמֵת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second, alternative answer to the challenge of step 1, alongside the שרץ answer of step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case to a tool that cannot become impure, backed by a ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We assumed he slaughtered with a metal knife, which takes on the impurity of a מת.
steps.terutzMaskana: He used a reed stalk, which cannot become impure, so the meat stays pure even though he is impure from a מת.
steps.raayaObject: That slaughtering with a reed stalk is valid.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא 'בכל שוחטים, בין בצור בין בזכוכית בין בקרומית של קנה'.

steps.title: אביי: the משנה means even a כותי may slaughter, under supervision
steps.stepSummary: אביי reads the משנה differently: 'הכל שוחטין' includes even a כותי. That is only when a Jew stands over him. If the Jew just comes and goes, the כותי should not slaughter.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: This is what the משנה teaches. Everyone may slaughter, even a Samaritan. When is that? When a Jew stands over him. But if the Jew only goes out and comes in, he may not slaughter.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי starts a new way of understanding the whole משנה. In his reading, the משנה is talking about a כותי slaughtering, not an impure person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier the גמרא noticed that the משנה seems to contradict itself: 'everyone slaughters' sounds like it is allowed from the start, but 'their slaughter is valid' sounds like it is only OK after the fact. אביי solves this by explaining 'הכל שוחטין' as being about a כותי, who is allowed from the start only with constant supervision. Occasional checking is not enough.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it is teaching, introducing a new reading of the משנה
A Samaritan (Cuthean), whose reliability in מצוות is in question
In what case are these words said? This limits a rule to a specific situation
Standing over him, meaning supervising constantly
Going out and coming in, meaning only checking now and then

steps.whyThisMatters: This opens a whole new branch of the sugya. Supervision of a slaughterer who might not be reliable becomes the focus of the rest of the discussion.

phrases.english: Abaye said: This is what it teaches:
everyone may slaughter, even a Samaritan.
In what case are these words said?
When a Jew is standing over him,
but if the Jew goes out and comes in, he may not slaughter.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the impure-slaughterer explanation and offers a completely different reading of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A כותי may slaughter from the start only when a Jew supervises him constantly; with only occasional checking, he may not slaughter.

steps.title: The olive-bulk test when a כותי slaughtered unsupervised
steps.stepSummary: Continuing אביי's reading: if the כותי slaughtered without supervision, give him an olive-bulk of the meat. If he eats it, the meat is permitted. If he doesn't, it is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if he did slaughter, the Jew cuts an olive-bulk of meat and gives it to him. If he ate it, it is permitted to eat from his slaughter. If he did not eat it, it is forbidden to eat from his slaughter.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי continues his reading and explains what happens after the fact, when a כותי already slaughtered without proper supervision. There is a simple test.
steps.deeperAnalysis: כותים are careful about the meat they themselves eat. So if the כותי is willing to eat from this animal, he must believe he slaughtered it properly, and the Jew may rely on that. If he refuses, that suggests something went wrong, so the meat is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: An olive-bulk, a standard minimum measure of food
His slaughter, meaning the animal he slaughtered
Permitted / forbidden

steps.whatToRemember: According to אביי, a כותי slaughters from the start only under constant supervision. After the fact, unsupervised meat can be permitted if the כותי himself eats an olive-bulk of it.

phrases.english: And if he slaughtered,
phrases.notes: He means a כותי who slaughtered when the Jew was only coming and going.

phrases.english: the Jew cuts an olive-bulk of meat and gives it to him.
If he ate it, it is permitted to eat from his slaughter;
if he did not eat it, it is forbidden to eat from his slaughter.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִם שָׁחַט, חוֹתֵךְ כְּזַיִת בָּשָׂר וְנוֹתֵן לוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues אביי's reading, moving from what is allowed from the start to what happens after the fact.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If a כותי slaughtered without supervision, give him an olive-bulk. If he eats it, the meat is permitted; if not, it is forbidden.

steps.title: Deaf-mute, imbecile and minor may never slaughter
steps.stepSummary: Continuing אביי's reading: a חרש, שוטה, and קטן may not slaughter even after the fact, because they may make classic שחיטה mistakes.
steps.simpleTranslation: Everyone may slaughter except a deaf-mute, an imbecile, and a minor. For them, even after the fact it does not work, because they might pause, press, or hide the knife.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes אביי's reading of the משנה. It adds the one group whose shechita is never valid: a חרש, a שוטה, and a קטן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a כותי, things can be fixed afterward, for example by the olive-bulk test. With these three, there is no fix at all. The worry is that they will make one of the mistakes that ruin a שחיטה: שהייה, דרסה, or חלדה.

keyTerms.meaning: A deaf-mute, a mentally incompetent person, and a minor
After the fact (once it was already done)
Pausing in the middle of the שחיטה
Pressing the knife down instead of drawing it back and forth
Hiding the knife under the skin or the pipes while cutting

phrases.english: except for a deaf-mute, an imbecile, and a minor,
for whom even after the fact it is also not valid,
lest they pause,
lest they press,
and lest they conceal (the knife).

steps.triggerLanguage: חוּץ מֵחֵרֵשׁ שׁוֹטֶה וְקָטָן, דַּאֲפִילּוּ דִּיעֲבַד נָמֵי לָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes אביי's line-by-line reading of the משנה that began in steps 4–5.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The shechita of a חרש, שוטה, or קטן is invalid even after the fact, because of the risk of שהייה, דרסה, or חלדה.

steps.title: What does 'and all of them who slaughtered' refer to?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which case the משנה's words 'וכולן ששחטו' refer to. It rules out the חרש, שוטה, and קטן, because then the wording should have been 'ואם שחטו'.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says 'and all of them who slaughtered.' Which case is that about? If you say it is about the deaf-mute, imbecile, and minor, since it sits right next to them, then it should have said 'and if they slaughtered'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests אביי's reading against another phrase in the משנה. It asks what 'וכולן ששחטו' (and all of them who slaughtered) is talking about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase sounds like a rule for after the fact. So it needs a case that is not allowed from the start. The obvious choice is the group right before it: the חרש, שוטה, and קטן. But the word 'כולן' (all of them) does not fit that group. The natural wording would have been 'ואם שחטו' (and if they slaughtered).

keyTerms.meaning: To which one? (which case is this referring to?)
If you say (the first suggestion, about to be pushed away)
It stands right next to it (it is the case just mentioned)
It should have said

phrases.english: "And all of them who slaughtered,"
to which case does it refer?
If you say it refers to the deaf-mute, imbecile, and minor,
since that is the case it stands next to,
it should have said "and if they slaughtered"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests אביי's reading from steps 4–6 against the next phrase of the משנה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The words 'וכולן ששחטו' must point to some case. The nearest case, the חרש, שוטה, and קטן, does not fit the word 'כולן'.

steps.title: It cannot refer to the כותי either, so the question stands
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tries to say the phrase refers to the כותי. But according to אביי, a כותי may slaughter even from the start when a Jew stands over him. So an after-the-fact phrase does not fit. The question is left unanswered.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it refers to the כותי? But you said that when a Jew stands over him, he may slaughter even from the start! This is difficult.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries a second option, the כותי, and rejects it too. It ends with 'קשיא', meaning the problem with אביי's reading remains.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'וכולן ששחטו' sounds like a rule for after the fact, when others watched. But אביי said that a כותי who is supervised may slaughter even from the start. So the phrase adds nothing for him. With both options gone, the wording stays a difficulty. It is not a full refutation of אביי.

keyTerms.meaning: A Samaritan
From the start (allowed to do it to begin with)
Standing over him (supervising)
It is difficult (an open problem, left unresolved)

steps.confusionAlert: 'קשיא' here means a difficulty that is left open. It is not a תיובתא (a full refutation), so אביי's reading is not thrown out.

phrases.english: Rather, it refers to the Samaritan?
But didn't you say:
when a Jew stands over him,
phrases.notes: This is אביי's own rule from step 4.

phrases.english: he may slaughter even from the start!
It is difficult.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries the second option after step 7 rejected the first, and finds it fails too.
steps.kashyaTarget: Reading 'וכולן ששחטו' as referring to the כותי
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A supervised כותי may already slaughter from the start, so a rule for after the fact would add nothing for him.

steps.title: רבא: a Jew going in and out should be enough
steps.stepSummary: רבא challenges אביי's rule that a כותי may not slaughter from the start when the Jew only goes in and out. He cites a משנה that permits leaving a נכרי in a store while a Jew goes in and out.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: When the Jew goes in and out, is it really not allowed from the start? But we learned: one who leaves a gentile in his store while a Jew goes in and out, it is permitted!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא attacks the part of אביי's rule from step 4 that says 'יוצא ונכנס' is not enough to allow shechita from the start.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה in עבודה זרה allows leaving a נכרי in a Jew's store while a Jew goes in and out. The gentile fears being caught at any moment, so he stays away from what is forbidden. רבא argues that the same fear should keep a כותי slaughtering properly. If so, it should be allowed even from the start.

keyTerms.meaning: Goes out and comes in (the Jew drops by now and then)
A gentile
Permitted

phrases.english: Rava said:
And when the Jew goes out and comes in, is it not allowed from the start?
But didn't we learn in a משנה:
one who leaves a gentile in his store
and a Jew goes out and comes in, it is permitted!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the wording problem and goes back to challenge אביי's rule about 'יוצא ונכנס' from step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's rule that a כותי may not slaughter from the start when the Jew only goes in and out
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A משנה treats a Jew who goes in and out as enough supervision for a נכרי, so it should also be enough for a כותי slaughtering.

steps.title: The store משנה is only about after the fact
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes away רבא's proof. The משנה says 'המניח' (one who left), not 'מניח' (one may leave). So it only permits the case after the fact.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, does it teach 'one may leave'? It teaches 'one who leaves,' which means after the fact.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends אביי by reading the store משנה's wording closely. It shows that the משנה does not allow 'יוצא ונכנס' from the start.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'מניח' would mean you may leave him there to begin with. 'המניח' describes someone who already did it. So the משנה only says that afterward the wine is permitted. It therefore does not contradict אביי, who said that a Jew going in and out is not enough for a כותי to slaughter from the start.

keyTerms.meaning: Does it teach? (a hint that it does not)
One may leave (from the start) / one who leaves (describes something already done)

steps.whatToRemember: According to אביי, a כותי may slaughter from the start only when a Jew stands over him. If the Jew only goes in and out and the כותי slaughtered, the meat depends on the כזית test. The store משנה does not refute this, because 'המניח' only describes after the fact. A חרש, שוטה, and קטן may never slaughter, even after the fact.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common method of the גמרא: the small difference between 'מניח' and 'המניח' decides whether a משנה allows something from the start or only after the fact.

phrases.english: There, does it teach "one may leave"?
It teaches "one who leaves," meaning after the fact.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof רבא brought in step 9.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects רבא's proof from the store משנה. The משנה itself stands; it just does not prove what רבא wanted.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רבא read the משנה as allowing this from the start, but its wording 'המניח' only describes what was already done.

steps.title: A stronger proof that going in and out is enough from the start
steps.stepSummary: רבא brings a new proof from a משנה about a guard watching wine. The guard does not need to sit there the whole time. Going in and out is permitted, which sounds like a rule for the start, not just after the fact.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, prove it from here: the guard does not need to be sitting and guarding. Even if he goes out and comes in, it is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: His first proof was pushed away, so רבא brings a better one. It shows that a Jew who only goes in and out is good enough even from the start.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier proof failed because 'המניח' only described something already done. This משנה says 'אין השומר צריך', the guard does not need to sit. That is a plain rule for how to act from the start. So it goes against אביי, who said going in and out works only after the fact.

keyTerms.meaning: from here, meaning from this source
a guard or watchman
goes out and comes in, so he is not there the whole time

phrases.english: Rather, from here:
phrases.notes: This is a משנה in עבודה זרה about a Jew watching wine that is kept with a non-Jew.

phrases.english: the guard does not need
to be sitting and guarding,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁיּוֹצֵא וְנִכְנָס – מוּתָּר.
phrases.english: rather, even though he goes out and comes in, it is permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the proof that was pushed away in step 10 with a stronger one.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's rule that a כותי may not slaughter from the start when the Jew only goes in and out.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A משנה about guarding wine says plainly that going in and out is enough. So it is enough from the start, not only after the fact.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in עבודה זרה about a guard over wine.

steps.title: רבא's own reading: a כותי may slaughter when a Jew goes in and out
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains the משנה in his own way. Everyone may slaughter, even a כותי, when a Jew goes in and out. If the Jew came later and found the animal already slaughtered, he gives the כותי a כזית of the meat. If the כותי eats it, the meat is permitted. If not, it is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: this is what the משנה teaches. Everyone may slaughter, even a כותי. When is this said? When a Jew goes in and out. But if the Jew came and found that he had already slaughtered, he cuts off a כזית of meat and gives it to him. If he eats it, one may eat from his slaughtering. If he does not eat it, one may not eat from his slaughtering.
steps.whatsHappening: Since going in and out is enough from the start, רבא gives a new reading of the משנה. It fits that rule, and it also covers the case where no Jew was there at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבא, a Jew going in and out is enough even from the start. The 'after the fact' case is now one where no Jew was around at all. Then the meat is checked with a test: the כותי eats a כזית from it, which shows he himself treats this slaughtering as kosher.

keyTerms.meaning: this is what the משנה is teaching, used to give a new reading of a source
a member of the Samaritan group, who keep some מצוות
in what case is this said? It limits the rule to a certain case
an olive-sized amount
his slaughtering, meaning the meat he slaughtered

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a second full way of reading the משנה, next to אביי's. It gives a practical test for meat a כותי slaughtered with no Jew present.

phrases.english: Rather, רבא said,
this is what it teaches:
Everyone may slaughter, and even a כותי.
In what case is this said?
When a Jew goes out and comes in,
but if he came and found that he had slaughtered,
he cuts off a כזית of meat and gives it to him,
if he ate it, it is permitted to eat from his slaughtering,
if he did not eat it, it is forbidden to eat from his slaughtering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the proof in step 11 and gives a new reading of the משנה in place of אביי's.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the משנה with different cases for the start and after the fact.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Following אביי, a Jew who only goes in and out is good only after the fact.
steps.terutzMaskana: Going in and out is enough from the start. The after-the-fact case is when no Jew was there at all, and then a כזית test is used.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A כותי may slaughter from the start if a Jew goes in and out. If no Jew was present, the meat is permitted only if the כותי eats a כזית of it.

steps.title: In רבא's reading too, a חרש, שוטה, and קטן are invalid even after the fact
steps.stepSummary: רבא's reading goes on. The rule does not include a חרש, שוטה, and קטן. Their slaughtering is invalid even after the fact, because they may make one of the classic שחיטה mistakes.
steps.simpleTranslation: Except for a חרש, a שוטה, and a קטן, who may not slaughter even after the fact. Maybe they will pause, maybe they will press, and maybe they will hide the knife.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes laying out רבא's reading of the משנה. It covers the חרש, שוטה, and קטן part, the same way it did for אביי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like אביי, רבא reads 'חוץ' as leaving these three out completely, even after the fact. The concern is that they will make one of the mistakes that ruin a שחיטה: שהייה (pausing), דרסה (pressing), or חלדה (hiding the knife). This sets up the same wording question about 'וכולן ששחטו'.

keyTerms.meaning: maybe they will pause in the middle of the cut, a mistake called שהייה
maybe they will press the knife down instead of drawing it, a mistake called דרסה
maybe they will hide the knife under the skin or pipes while cutting, a mistake called חלדה

phrases.english: except for a deaf-mute, an imbecile, and a minor,
for whom even after the fact it is also not valid,
lest they pause, and lest they press,
and lest they hide the knife.

steps.triggerLanguage: חוּץ מֵחֵרֵשׁ שׁוֹטֶה וְקָטָן, דַּאֲפִילּוּ דִּיעֲבַד נָמֵי לָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רבא's reading from step 12, the same way step 6 continued אביי's.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A חרש, שוטה, and קטן may not slaughter, even after the fact.

steps.title: What does 'וכולן ששחטו' refer to? Not the חרש, שוטה, and קטן
steps.stepSummary: Now the גמרא asks רבא the same question it asked אביי: which case do the words 'וכולן ששחטו' refer to? It cannot be the חרש, שוטה, and קטן, even though they come right before. If it were, the משנה should have said 'ואם שחטו'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And 'all of them who slaughtered', which case is this about? If you say it is about the חרש, שוטה, and קטן, which it stands next to, then it should have said 'and if they slaughtered'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests רבא's reading against the next words in the משנה. It starts by ruling out the first possible case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'וכולן ששחטו' talks about something done after the fact. In רבא's reading, the only nearby group is the חרש, שוטה, and קטן. But the word 'וכולן' (all of them) does not fit that, since a separate case would be written 'ואם שחטו'.

keyTerms.meaning: about which one? Which case does this refer to?
it stands next to it, the text right beside it
it should have said

phrases.english: And 'all of them who slaughtered', to which case does it refer?
If you say to the deaf-mute, imbecile, and minor,
since it stands next to it,
it should have said 'and if they slaughtered'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Puts רבא's reading to the same wording test used on אביי in step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's reading of the משנה, as it relates to the phrase 'וכולן ששחטו'.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The word 'וכולן' does not fit a single group that was just mentioned. That would be written 'ואם שחטו'.

steps.title: It cannot refer to the כותי either, so רבא's reading is left difficult
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tries to say the phrase refers to the כותי. But רבא himself said a כותי may slaughter from the start even when a Jew only goes in and out. So an after-the-fact phrase does not fit, and the question stays unanswered.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it refers to the כותי? But you said that even when the Jew goes in and out, he may slaughter from the start! It is difficult.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries the second option, the כותי. It finds that this does not fit רבא's own rule, and ends with 'קשיא', an unanswered difficulty.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רבא's reading, a Jew going in and out already lets a כותי slaughter from the start. So the watching described in 'וכולן ששחטו' is not an after-the-fact case for a כותי. Neither option works, so the wording stays a problem for רבא, just as it did for אביי.

keyTerms.meaning: but you said, used to point back to the speaker's own rule
from the start, before acting
it is difficult, a question left without an answer

steps.confusionAlert: This looks just like step 8, but it is a different problem. For אביי, the issue was a Jew standing over the כותי. For רבא, it goes further: even a Jew going in and out is enough from the start.
steps.whatToRemember: Both אביי and רבא read the משנה in a way that leaves 'וכולן ששחטו' without a clear case. In both readings it ends with קשיא.

phrases.english: Rather, to the כותי?
But you said:
even when he goes out and comes in,
he may slaughter from the start!
It is difficult.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rules out the second option after step 14 ruled out the first, and leaves the question open.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's reading of the משנה, as it relates to the phrase 'וכולן ששחטו'.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In רבא's reading, a כותי may already slaughter from the start when a Jew goes in and out. So an after-the-fact phrase cannot be about him.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The wording 'וכולן ששחטו' stays a difficulty for רבא's reading.

steps.title: רב אשי reads the משנה as including a ישראל משומד
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי offers a new reading: the משנה's 'everyone slaughters' even includes a ישראל משומד.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: This is what the משנה is teaching. Everyone may slaughter, and even a Jew who is a משומד.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי gives a brand-new way to read the משנה, since the readings of אביי and רבא ran into questions. He says the word 'הכל' (everyone) even reaches a ישראל משומד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The basic problem was that the משנה seems to say 'from the start' (הכל שוחטין) and also 'after the fact' (ושחיטתן כשרה). רב אשי starts a new explanation by putting a new person into 'הכל': a ישראל משומד. Exactly how this solves the problem is not spelled out yet; the גמרא first needs to define what kind of משומד he means.

keyTerms.meaning: 'This is what it teaches,' a phrase used to give a new reading of a משנה
'Everyone slaughters,' the opening words of the משנה
A Jew who regularly breaks a certain מצוה

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
This is what the mishna is teaching:
Everyone slaughters,
and even a Jewish transgressor.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the question on רבא stayed unanswered, a third אמורא offers a different reading of the משנה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה's 'from the start' wording (הכל שוחטין) and 'after the fact' wording (ושחיטתן כשרה) seemed to clash, and the readings of אביי and רבא left 'וכולן ששחטו' without a fitting case.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'הכל שוחטין' is read as including even a ישראל משומד.

steps.title: What kind of משומד?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which kind of sin makes this person a משומד.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for a definition: what does this person do that makes him a משומד? This question sets up the next step's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Not every משומד is the same. Someone who rejects a מצוה to rebel is very different from someone who breaks it for convenience. The answer will decide whether his שחיטה can be trusted.

keyTerms.meaning: 'For what?' asking what exactly is meant

phrases.english: A transgressor of what sort?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for a definition of the משומד that רב אשי just mentioned.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which kind of sin makes this person a משומד in רב אשי's reading.

steps.title: One who eats נבילות for convenience
steps.stepSummary: The משומד here is someone who eats נבילות לתיאבון, out of appetite or convenience.
steps.simpleTranslation: One who is a משומד in eating נבילות for his appetite.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers: this משומד eats נבילות (animals not slaughtered properly) only because it is easier or he wants them, not to rebel.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'לתיאבון' means his sin comes from desire, not from rejecting the תורה. Such a person would not choose a forbidden animal if a kosher one were just as easy. This detail is what will make his שחיטה acceptable.

keyTerms.meaning: Animals that died without a kosher shechita
Out of appetite or convenience, not out of rebellion

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think this משומד sins to anger God. 'לתיאבון' means he does it only for convenience, which is very different from a משומד להכעיס (one who sins to rebel).

phrases.english: To eat unslaughtered animal carcasses to satisfy his appetite,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the question of what kind of משומד is meant.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A משומד who eats נבילות לתיאבון, out of convenience and not rebellion.

steps.title: This matches a ruling of רבא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says this fits רבא's ruling about a ישראל משומד who eats נבילות לתיאבון. רבא's words begin here and continue in the next part.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this is like רבא, for רבא said: A Jewish משומד who eats נבילות for his appetite...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up רב אשי's reading by pointing to a ruling of רבא about this exact kind of משומד. Only the opening of רבא's statement appears here; the ruling itself comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אשי's reading is not invented on the spot; it lines up with an existing ruling of רבא. The case described is exactly the person from the last step. What רבא rules about his shechita is still to come.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And like רבא,' showing this fits his known ruling

phrases.english: And in accordance with the statement of Rava,
as Rava says:
A Jewish transgressor
who eats unslaughtered animal carcasses to satisfy his appetite

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the definition just given by linking it to a known ruling of רבא.
steps.raayaObject: רב אשי's reading that 'הכל שוחטין' includes a משומד לתיאבון
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבא's statement about a ישראל משומד who eats נבילות לתיאבון (continues on the next amud)
